tre by a strong encounter with the SMBH.

The recently discovered hypervelocity star SDSS J090745.0+024507
(hereafter HVS) is escaping the Galaxy at high speed and could be the first object in
this class.

We confirm the prediction by Hills (1988) and
Yu & Tremaine (2003) that dynamical encounters with the
SMBH can eject hypervelocity stars to the Galactic halo;
the HVS is likely the first discovered object of this kind.

notes: SDSS J090745.0+024507 (called “HVS” throughout; T:p1-b5) is the only actual star studied. It was announced as a hypervelocity star by Brown et al. (2005; T:p1-b8), so this targeted origin study is recorded as follow-up; the paper also describes it as escaping the Galaxy and retains that assessment at T:p5-b10. The scattering simulations concern generic stars, not additional identifiable objects.

SDSS J090745.0+024507: The proper-motion entries are not independent measured components; Table 1 reports average model proper motions, for each adopted distance, that make the backward-traced orbit pass within d_min < 10 pc of the Galactic centre. The paper also states that a proper motion of about 2 mas/yr is required to come within a few pc of the SMBH, but this is not a separate component value. No explicit RA, Dec, parallax, present-day galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported. The 730 km/s value relative to the Local Standard of Rest is excluded by the rules. The V_ej values in Table 1 are ejection velocities at d_min, not present-day Galactic-rest-frame velocities, so they are not included.
